newsitem.title: USA: DTE Energy could see charge from storm.
newsitem.headline: DTE Energy could see charge from storm.

text.p: DTE Energy Co said Monday a major storm July 2 could lead to a charge on 1997 earnings of up to about $24 million.
The storm resulted in about $36 million in damage to the electrical system, the company said.
The company also said an increase in second quarter net income was due primarily to higher electric sales and lower maintenance expenses.
Several developments contributed to increased operating revenues in the second quarter and are expected to have a favorable impact on earnings in future periods, the company said.
Repairs at Fermi 2 nuclear power plant were completed and the plant has been operating at more than 90 percent power, the company said.

DTE Energy also announced its acquisition of National Steel Corp's coke oven battery; the formation of DTE-CoEnergy LLC, a joint venture with MCN Energy Group Inc; and its investment in Plug Power LLC, a joint venture to develop and manufacture fuel cells.

"While we had a minor storm in April which caused about $7 million in damage and mild weather in May, we still had a decent quarter," Anthony Earley Jr, DTE Energy president and chief operating officer, said in a news release. "Our profit level is a reflection of continued aggressive cost control across the board. We continue to look for every opportunity to drive waste out of our processes."
Earlier Monday, the company reported net income of $84.9 million, or $0.59 a share, for the second quarter, compared to $78.3 million, or $0.54 a share, a year ago.
